keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, shape taken from the Kingdom row: Cliopatria's Socialist Republic row begins in 1948 but the page dates the end of the monarchy to the 'forced abdication of Michael I: 30 December 1947', when the People's Republic was proclaimed. The shape therefore overlaps the kingdom-of-romania 1947 shape (written by eu-21) for the whole of 1947; that dossier should end its shape in December. The page gives no area, so the infobox comparison is unverified: page budget.

238,172 km2 for 1948-1986; the outline is identical to the Kingdom's 1947 shape and to the Romania row of 1990. The peace treaties (signed 10 February 1947, effective 15 September 1947) 'giving Northern Transylvania back to Romania' (the Vienna Award void), left the 1940 losses of Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina to the Soviet Union and 'returned Southern Dobruja to Bulgaria'; the frontiers then stand unchanged to 1989. Area: unverified: page budget (the Socialist Republic page gives none).
Same outline as 1948 (238,172 km2). The page reports no frontier change in 1965 (the Socialist Republic constitution) or in the revolution of December 1989. Area: unverified: page budget.

ledger.note: 1947: the monarchy ends and the People's Republic begins. Infobox 'Forced abdication of Michael I: 30 December 1947'; the text has Parliament abolish the monarchy and proclaim a republic the same day, and 'from 1947 to 1965 it was the Romanian People's Republic'. The page gives the date, not a frontier.

1965: the Romanian People's Republic becomes the Socialist Republic of Romania. 'On 21 August 1965 the country's name was changed to Socialist Republic of Romania' (the 1965 constitution is dated the same day). Colour and dossier continue.

region.text: the whole country, which keeps its outline as Romania

ledger.note: 1989: Ceaușescu falls and the Socialist Republic ends. The fall is dated 22 December 1989, Ceaușescu was executed on 25 December, 'the name was changed to Romania on 28 December 1989'; the page also gives 8 December 1991 for the state's formal abolition, which is not applied.

certainty.note: Treaty frontiers of 1947 (Northern Transylvania restored, Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina to the Soviet Union, Southern Dobruja to Bulgaria), unchanged to 1989; the pages opened give no survey detail.

notes: Cliopatria draws this row 1948-1989 with one outline (the same as the Kingdom of Romania's 1947 shape and the 1990 Romania row), so the state is a no-boundary-change case; the work was to date its start (30 December 1947 abdication of Michael I, People's Republic proclaimed), its rename (21 August 1965) and its end (name changed to Romania on 28 December 1989, the successor Romania dossier founds in December 1989). The 1947 keyframe is new and overlaps the Kingdom's 1947 shape: eu-21's kingdom-of-romania dossier should end its 1947 shape before the People's Republic (or the compiler resolve the overlap in favour of the later state). Wikidata Q203493 sits on the Kingdom and Romania rows, not on this one (Q842794), so no merge question arises. Not on the pages opened: the infobox area (so the comparison with 238,172 km2 is unverified: page budget); the Soviet occupation start ('Soviet troops occupied the country after the war', no date; withdrawal 'by 1958'), which is not a territorial event; the Allied Control Commission; the formal-abolition date 8 December 1991 given on the page contradicts the December 1989 end and is not applied. Leaders are not listed as rulers because the infobox list starts in 1952. Gazetteer names: none missing.
